title: 'Document Classes'
subtitle: 'The 16-class RVL-CDIP target vocabulary'
toc: true
toc-depth: 3
---

::: {.callout-note title="The 16-Class Taxonomy"}
The classifier distinguishes between these 16 RVL-CDIP document classes. They are the
target vocabulary for the **exact-match accuracy metric** and the rows/columns of every
confusion matrix on this site. A prediction is scored correct **only if it exactly matches**
the ground-truth class name (case-insensitive).
:::

| # | Class | Notes |
|---|-------|-------|
| 1 | `advertisement` | Promotional and marketing materials |
| 2 | `budget` | Financial planning, estimates, campaign contributions |
| 3 | `email` | Mail-client formatted messages (From/To/Sent/Subject) |
| 4 | `file_folder` | Identifier-only pages: Bates stamps, stickers, labels |
| 5 | `form` | Administrative data-capture with fields, boxes, approval blocks |
| 6 | `handwritten` | Majority freeform handwriting carrying the main message |
| 7 | `invoice` | Payment demands, billing documents, vendor estimates |
| 8 | `letter` | External correspondence with salutation and closing signature |
| 9 | `memo` | Internal correspondence (TO:/FROM:/RE: headers, no external address) |
| 10 | `news_article` | Newspaper/magazine editorial content with masthead |
| 11 | `presentation` | Slide decks, covers, company statements |
| 12 | `questionnaire` | Survey instruments with rating scales, multiple choice, open-response |
| 13 | `resume` | CV, career history, biographical sketches (including PHS 398) |
| 14 | `scientific_publication` | Published journal articles with volume/issue/page headers |
| 15 | `scientific_report` | Research write-ups, lab results, study findings |
| 16 | `specification` | Product/material documentation, MSDS, "shall/must" requirements |

::: {.callout-warning title="Most Common Confusion Pairs"}
Across all experiments, the dominant confusion pairs are:
- **`letter` ↔ `memo`** — correspondence header ambiguity (internal vs. external)
- **`budget` ↔ `invoice`** — financial document function (planning vs. billing)
- *** → `form`** — structured layouts with fields/approval blocks over-attract the `form` label
:::
